slides.title: A partner bio should sell, [not list a CV].
slides.lede: Buyers check bios to see whether a firm's claims hold up. The first sentence should say who the partner helps, and with what.

slides.title: Name the [clients and the work] before the qualifications
slides.text: Buyers and search engines read the first sentence most closely. Years of experience and qualifications work better later in the bio.

slides.title: What the grader [scores out of 100]
slides.note: Each check comes with a specific fix, and **the clichés are marked in the text**.

slides.title: Numbers buyers can verify, [not bare dates]

cards.label: Counts
cards.text: Deal sizes, numbers of matters, years in a sector.

cards.label: Doesn't count
cards.text: A bare date such as "qualified in 2003".

slides.title: Checked against [326 stock phrases] and clichés

items.title: Wealth of experience
items.text: A common biography cliché the grader marks.

items.title: Passionate about
items.text: Tells a buyer nothing about the work.

items.title: Trusted adviser
items.text: Every firm in your sector claims it.

slides.title: 100 to 300 words, in [one consistent person]
slides.text: Keep longer versions with full matter lists for proposals and directory submissions. Switching between first and third person costs points.

slides.title: Grade three or four bios for a fair picture.
slides.lede: Partner Bio Grader: free, and nothing you paste leaves your browser. Find out more via the link in our bio.
